I've had this phone for a few months now and am now ready to review it, I'll break down this review into build quality, screen quality, weight, audio quality/call quality, processor speed, camera quality, battery life and ease of navigating the software. - Build quality is outstanding, the phone looks and feels as good as it gets.The phone is a little slippery though so I do recommend a case for it, more on that later. -Screen quality- This is by far the best display I have ever seen on a phone, samsungs amoled display technology is at the top of its game. Colors pop,contrast is incredible and the blacks are truly black and because of the curved screen the content you view on it whether its photos or videos has an almost 3d effect to it.

Galaxy S8 Review. Upon owning the Galaxy S8 for a month, I feel ready to give it a review. This phone is a great choice for any Android (operating system) user. The reason this phone is a great fit for Android users is that it is physically the same size as many competitor phones, but the screen is larger. This means users get the best of both worlds; a phone small enough to fit in the pocket, and a large screen. Review Criteria When reviewing a phone, I consider physical appearance, storage capacity, battery life, and how well the phone does what it is supposed to do. This device is visually appealing. If you have had a previous Galaxy, you may recall the only option for black had a distinct blue tinge to it. The S8 is a true black, and it looks much better than the old option.

Great Phone. The screen on this phone is something to be desired by all. It has a beautiful screen that can display the phenomenal pictures this phone takes. It is a fast and reliable product. I highly recommend this phone!

Screen Burned. Great phone, however it was screen burned with the "always on" time screen. Its faint but noticable on white screens, yet completely invsible on dark screens. The screen was not damaged physically. I would recommend to anyone wanting a good phone with a possible risk of faint screen burn. Sometimes I forget its there.

Pro: Decent Camera, good with low light environment. Great Battery life, 3500 amh, last longer then any other phone I had in the past. Support wireless charging, water-proof. Less overheating. a pretty "status symbol" phone with lots of disappointments.. My first Android was a OnePlus One. Then, a One Plus Two. I have zero complaints about these two phones. The screen on my OP2 cracked, so I decided to splurge and got myself this beauty. In retrospect, I should have just repaired my OP2's screen. The S8 was an absolute (and expensive) disappointment. It gives you gimmicky features such as the iris-scan, the heart-rate monitor, edge-lighting, which are honestly a bit useless, in my opinion. The curved screen, while a novelty, is incredibly pointless, and in fact creates glare at the edges which makes it very hard to see notifications when the phone is mounted in your car. A lot of people are annoyed about the finger-print scanner's location. It's not ideal, but I've tolerated it and it seems to work okay for me.

Screen cracked in 3 days - design is flawed!. I've had just about every Samsung Galaxy phone since S2. Loved it. Always a step ahead of Apple and I liked the flexibility of Android. Bought S8 and I had to say it is the worst Galaxy I've owned. The main issue is screen that cracks SO easily. I didn't even drop the phone, I sat down and it was in my pocket, and the little bump of the phone caused the screen to crack. In a few more days I got a few more cracks. There is absolutely no value in the "infinity" screen, it's beautiful but worthless. In my 8 years of owning multiple Galaxies I only cracked the screen once, and I dropped it many times. S8 has a design flaw. Then there's Samsung bloatware that annoys the hell out of you. Bixby is useless but you can't disable it.
